title: Standard affine fpqc covers are quotient maps
statement: Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{f_j:V_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j)\to T\}_{j\in J}$ be a finite family with $R\to\prod_{j\in J}A_j$ faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. For a subset $W\subseteq T$, if every inverse image $f_j^{-1}(W)\subseteq V_j$ is open, then $W$ is open in $T$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JY (morphisms-lemma-fpqc-quotient-topology), applied to the coproduct of the finite standard fpqc family

proof.text: Put $B=\prod_{j\in J}A_j$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$. The finite coproduct $\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ is identified with $V$ by the canonical finite-product spectrum isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum]; its coprojections are open, pairwise disjoint, and cover $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (4), [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Let $g:V\to T$ be the morphism induced by $R\to B$; under this identification $g$ restricts to $f_j$ on the $j$-th summand.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, affine reduction and finite standard covering; Morphisms Lemma Tag 02JY setup

proof.text: The morphism $g$ is flat because the faithfully flat map $R\to B$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and flatness of an affine spectrum morphism is equivalent to flatness of its ring map [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. It is quasi-compact because it is affine and affine morphisms are quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3). Finally $g$ is surjective because the faithfully flat map $R\to B$ induces a surjection $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum].

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JY proof, affine case, with Algebra Lemma Tag 00HQ for faithful-flat surjectivity

proof.text: Apply the quotient-map statement [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map] to $g$. It gives that $W$ is open in $T$ if and only if $g^{-1}(W)$ is open in $V$.

Because the coprojection images are open and cover $V$, the inverse image $g^{-1}(W)$ is open exactly when its intersection with every summand is open; these intersections are the inverse images $f_j^{-1}(W)$. The hypothesis therefore makes $g^{-1}(W)$ open, and Step 3 yields that $W$ is open in $T$.
